exposure: Outpatient cervical ripening using mechanical methods (osmotic dilators and Foley balloon)
outcome: Maternal outcomes (cervical dilation, simplified bishop scores, time from admission to delivery, total length of stay, hours of oxytocin use, mode of delivery, maternal complications)
cohort: The study included 391 patients (116 outpatient, 275 inpatient) with low-risk, term, singleton pregnancies who underwent cervical ripening.
finding: Outpatient cervical ripening using multiple mechanical methods was associated with significantly higher cervical dilation, shorter average time from patient admission to delivery, and shorter total length of stay for vaginal deliveries.
mod_finding: Mode of delivery did not differ between the outpatient and inpatient cervical ripening groups.
